formats.key: Order(address maker,Asset makeAsset,address taker,Asset takeAsset,uint256 salt,uint256 start,uint256 end,bytes4 dataType,bytes data)Asset(AssetType assetType,uint256 value)AssetType(bytes4 assetClass,bytes data)
effects: Signing lets anyone (or only `taker` when it is non-zero) match the order. The make asset then leaves the signer's wallet through Rarible transfer proxies, using approvals the signer already gave, up to makeAsset.value. The order can be filled in parts.
The signer gets the take asset in proportion to the fill. It goes to the payout addresses encoded in `data`, and only to the maker when `data` lists no payouts.

When the signer sells an NFT for ETH or ERC20, the payment they get is cut first. Royalties from the RoyaltiesRegistry, the origin fees of both orders (from `data`) and, for V3 data, the seller protocol fee are taken out of the take amount.
When the signer pays with ERC20 or ETH, the origin fees in their own `data` (and the buyer protocol fee for V3) are added on top of makeAsset.value.
The order can be filled only after `start` and before `end`. `end` = 0 means it never expires. It stays fillable until fully filled or cancelled on chain.
formats.shown: A generic 'Exchange order' title, then the maker and taker addresses, the make and take asset kinds as enum names, both amounts as raw integers, the asset data as raw hex, and the start and end dates when they are non-zero. The order data (payouts and fees) is hidden.

findings.title: Order: `data` is hidden (visible: never), so payout recipients and origin fees that cut or add to amounts are never shown.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json field {"path":"data","visible":"never"}. LibOrderData.parse decodes payouts and originFees from order.data. In RaribleTransferManager.doTransfersWithFees, nftSide.originFees are paid out of the seller's proceeds, and calculateTotalAmount adds paymentSide.originFees on top of the buyer's amount. transferPayouts sends the proceeds to `payouts`, not necessarily the maker. Case 0: data has originFees [(0x1cf0df2a…e18a, 475 bp)], so 4.75% of the 0.075 ETH shown goes to a third party.
findings.fix: Show the order data, e.g. a visible 'Payouts and fees (encoded)' field, and label the take amount 'before fees'. Better: once the spec can decode bytes, show payouts and origin fees as their own fields.

findings.title: Order: 'Take asset amount' reads as what the seller gets, but royalties and fees are deducted first.
findings.evidence: RaribleTransferManager.doTransfersWithFees: rest = transferProtocolFee(...); rest = transferRoyalties(... royaltiesRegistry.getRoyalties(token, tokenId) ...); then transferFees for origin fees; transferPayouts(paymentSide.asset.assetType, rest, ...). Case 0 and case 2 are sell orders that show 'Take asset amount' 75000000000000000 and 4100000000000000000 with no mention of deductions.
findings.fix: Rename the label to 'Price before royalties and fees' and say in the intent that royalties and marketplace fees are taken from the payment.

findings.title: Order: make and take amounts are raw integers with no token, decimals or unit.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json makeAsset.value and takeAsset.value use "format":"raw". Case 0 shows 'Take asset amount' 75000000000000000 (0.075 ETH). Case 3 shows 'Make asset amount' 70000000000000000 for WETH.
findings.fix: Use amount/tokenAmount where the class allows it: tokenPath on makeAsset.assetType.data.[12:32] for ERC20 and nativeCurrencyAddress for ETH. Otherwise label the field 'amount in smallest units'.

findings.title: Order: asset data is shown as raw ABI hex that hides the NFT contract, token ID or ERC20 address.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json makeAsset.assetType.data and takeAsset.assetType.data use "format":"raw". Case 0 shows 0x000…adf9c3c2d2946b3c80913b9e022dc2ce9e93afd9000…0a78 (contract 0xadf9…, token id 2680). TransferExecutor.transfer decodes it as (address token, uint tokenId).
findings.fix: Add sliced fields: an 'Asset contract' field on assetType.data.[12:32] with addressName or token, and a 'Token ID' field on assetType.data.[32:64].

findings.title: Order: the intent 'Exchange order' does not say what the signer gives or gets, and there is no interpolated intent.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json "intent": "Exchange order", interpolatedIntent absent. The labels 'Make asset' and 'Take asset' are protocol jargon. Case 0 is a sale of an NFT and case 3 is a WETH collection bid, and both read the same.
findings.fix: Use an intent like 'Sign Rarible order: give asset for asset', with an interpolatedIntent that names the make kind and amount and the take kind and amount. Relabel 'Make' as 'You give' and 'Take' as 'You receive'.

findings.title: Order: `end` = 0 hides the expiry field even though it means the order never expires, and zero taker means anyone.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json end has visible ifNotIn [0,'0']. LibOrder.validateOrderTime: require(order.end == 0 || order.end > block.timestamp). Cases 0, 2 and 3 show taker 0x0000…0000 raw, and validateOrders skips the taker check when taker == address(0).
findings.fix: Always show end, with a message such as 'Never expires' for 0. Show taker as addressName with a 'Anyone' label for the zero address.

findings.title: Order: the Polygon deployment 0x7f19…aa53 is a RoyaltiesRegistry, not the Rarible exchange.
findings.evidence: contracts/137-0x7f19564c35c681099c0c857a7141836cf7edaa53/meta.json: fullyQualifiedName RoyaltiesRegistry.sol:RoyaltiesRegistry, not a proxy. descriptor.json deployments include {chainId:137, address:0x7f19564c…}.
findings.fix: Replace the chain-137 entry with the Polygon ExchangeV2 proxy address that verifies 'Exchange' v2 orders.

couldNotCheck: LibOrderDataV1/V2/V3 sources are omitted from the ExchangeV2 implementation (1-0xa669…3782), so I could not confirm which version dataType 0x4ade54ca is. That decides whether the protocol fee applies to cases 0, 2 and 3.

The mainnet RoyaltiesRegistry and transfer proxies the exchange calls at runtime (their addresses are in storage) are not in the directory. They decide the royalty cut taken from the seller's proceeds.

findings.title: Order: 'Take asset amount' reads as what the seller gets, but royalties and fees are deducted first.
findings.reason: For a sell order, the ETH take side is the fee side. Before the seller's payout, doTransfersWithFees takes out the protocol fee (only the buyer's share for these V2 orders), the royalties from the registry, and the seller's origin fees. The screen shows only the full 'Take asset amount' (75000000000000000 and 4100000000000000000) and says nothing about these deductions. The guide's amount rule makes this critical: royalties are read from storage, but they cut the amount shown. In case 0, the 4.75% origin fee makes the cut a fact.
